I farm a small wheat-maize rotation on 6.5 mu, and I would keep that full rotation on all my land this year because that is the system I know best and it fits my well irrigation and my family labor situation. I have farmed for 30 years, so I would not do anything fancy or risky. I would use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize because I want stable emergence, stronger yield, and better resistance. Since some family members work off-farm, I would keep management practical: medium fertilizer rates, a limited number of irrigations, and only the pesticide sprays I expect I will really need. For wheat, I would focus on a solid base fertilizer, one or two irrigations at key stages, and careful weed and disease control because wheat yield depends on steady early management. For maize, I would put more emphasis on nitrogen, use fewer irrigations because summer rain helps, and spray only if pest pressure appears. I would use rotary tillage because it is fast, familiar, and workable on my small area under a wheat-maize system.
